stemMd: For real x, the absolute value of 2x−1 is 7. What is the product of the possible values of x?
explanationMd: Solve 2x−1=7 and 2x−1=−7 to get x=4 and x=−3. Their product is −12. Both values reproduce absolute value 7.

distractorRationale.c: This squares only the positive root.
distractorRationale.b: This uses the absolute-value target as a root.
distractorRationale.d: This is their sum, not product.
